notes:
Summary: Equinox Grove is a mid-market SaaS company (product discovery + personalized recommendations) evaluating Redwood Hosted API as a fast POC path, then moving to Dedicated in EU for production. Key ask: EU-only data residency for production tokens and logs, with multi-region routing only for failover (must be opt-in).

POC details:
- Hosted API POC (2 weeks) running embeddings + reranking for product search. Peak 200 req/s, average session length ~18 tokens per request.
- Observed latency: p95 ~170ms from Frankfurt during POC; engineering asks if Dedicated in eu-west can hit p95 <= 150ms for gen+rerank workloads.
- Cost sensitivity: target ARR range 75k-200k; preference for batching and quantized model suggestions from Redwood Optimize to bring per-token cost down.

Security & Compliance:
- Must meet EU data residency (customer data not to leave EU for production). Trial POC ok to run in hosted global, but production must be VPC/Dedicated EU only.
- Requirements: SSO (SAML), audit logging retained 1 year, KMS integration for key control, SOC2 compliance language in contract.

Routing & HA conversation:
- Equinox prefers single-region primary (eu-west) + optional async failover to na for disaster recovery. Concern: routing latency tradeoffs vs cost.
- Wants clear SLA for regional failover and a policy that failover is only used when primary unreachable. Requests documented routing policy examples.

Quotes / paraphrases:
- "We want production data to stay in EU — dev/test can be flexible, but we need guarantees for prod." — Lena V., CTO.
- "If Dedicated gives us predictable latency and cost, we'll commit to 1yr reserved capacity." — Head of Platform (A. Romero).

Open items:
- Confirm Dedicated EU p95 latency targets on recommended instance types and model variants.
- Provide sample pricing for 1yr reserved Dedicated (baseline + tiers) and variable burst pricing.
- Legal: finalize DPA + data residency appendix; confirm audit log retention terms.
